q: Arunachal Pradesh: The Tawang Monastery, the largest monastery in India, belongs to which sect?
e: Tawang Monastery, founded in the 17th century, belongs to the Gelug school.

q: Manipur: The Manipuri classical dance is chiefly based on themes of:
o: The Ras Lila of Radha and Krishna
e: Manipuri dance centres on the Ras Lila depicting Radha, Krishna and the gopis.

q: Manipur: Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park, lies in which lake?
e: Keibul Lamjao floats on phumdis in Loktak Lake.

q: Meghalaya: Mawsynram, near Cherrapunji, is famous for being:
o: One of the wettest places on Earth
e: Mawsynram in the Khasi Hills receives among the highest average rainfall in the world.

q: Meghalaya: The 'living root bridges' of Meghalaya are made by the Khasi and Jaintia people from:
e: Living root bridges are grown by guiding aerial roots of Ficus elastica.

q: Mizoram: Cheraw, performed by dancers stepping between clapping bamboo poles, is a famous dance of:
e: Cheraw (bamboo dance) is the best-known traditional dance of Mizoram.

q: Nagaland: The Hornbill Festival, held every December at Kisama, is a showcase of:
e: The Hornbill Festival celebrates the heritage of all Naga tribes.

q: Sikkim: In which year did Sikkim become a state of India?
e: Sikkim became the 22nd state of India in 1975.

q: Arunachal Pradesh: Ziro Valley is the homeland of which tribe, known for sustainable rice-fish farming?
e: The Apatani of Ziro practise wet rice cultivation combined with fish farming.

q: Arunachal Pradesh: Namdapha National Park is notable for hosting four big cats: tiger, leopard, clouded leopard and:
e: Namdapha in Changlang district is the only park in India with all four of these big cats.

q: Manipur: The Sangai, the state animal of Manipur, is a:
e: The Sangai is an endangered brow-antlered deer found in Keibul Lamjao.

q: Meghalaya: Wangala, a post-harvest festival honouring the sun god Saljong, is celebrated by the:
e: Wangala, known as the 'Hundred Drums Festival', is the main festival of the Garos.

q: Nagaland: Nagaland became a state of India on:
e: Nagaland was inaugurated as the 16th state on 1 December 1963.

q: Sikkim: Khangchendzonga National Park is India's first UNESCO World Heritage Site of which category?
e: Khangchendzonga National Park was inscribed in 2016 as India's first mixed heritage site.

q: Sikkim: The Rumtek Monastery near Gangtok is the seat of which school of Tibetan Buddhism?
e: Rumtek is the main seat of the Karma Kagyu lineage in exile.

q: Tripura: The Ujjayanta Palace, a former royal palace, is located in:
e: Ujjayanta Palace in Agartala was built by Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya around 1901.

q: Tripura: The Neermahal water palace stands in which lake?
e: Neermahal was built by Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya in Rudrasagar Lake.

q: Meghalaya: Nongkrem, a five-day thanksgiving dance festival, is celebrated by the:
e: The Nongkrem festival is held by the Khasi people at Smit near Shillong.

q: Tripura: Unakoti is famous for its:
o: Buddhist stupas of the Mauryan age
e: Unakoti in north Tripura has huge rock-cut images, especially of Shiva.

q: Which two states attained statehood on 20 February 1987?
e: Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram became states on 20 February 1987; Goa followed on 30 May 1987.
